newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS-Renault warns on loss, shares fall.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Renault warns on loss, shares fall.

text.p: French car and truck maker Renault issued a warning on Friday that its 1996 operating loss would be considerably higher than the market generally expected because of a difficult economic climate.
It also reported virtually flat turnover for the year at 184.1 billion francs ($32.3 billion) despite stronger revenues in the car division.
"The operating loss to be reported by Renault Group for 1996 will be considerably higher than that generally anticipated by the financial markets," Renault said in a statement.

This was "in view of the prevailing economic context, and despite the increase in revenues of the automobile division, reflecting a more positive trend which has been confirmed by a widening of the Renault market share in France in the early part of 1997", it said.
The company has previously issued warnings for 1996, saying both its car and truck operations would lose money.
Renault did not say what it considered to be the market's consensus forecast for its 1996 operating result.

But one analyst said the market had been expecting operating losses of roughly two billion francs for the car division and 600 million francs for trucks, plus an operating profit of around 1.3 billion at the finance unit. This would give a total operating loss of 1.3 billion francs.
He said he expected the car division's loss to be nearer 2.8 billion francs after the profit warning.
Renault shares ignored a slightly stronger stock market opening on Friday to start the day down 3.7 francs or 2.8 percent at 126.9 francs a share.

"Operating conditions for the Renault Automobile Division were negatively impacted by the spread throughout Europe, and more particularly in France, of relentless and aggressive price wars, which resulted in substantial increases in resources allocated for marketing," Renault said in its sales statement.
"Moreover the Commercial Vehicles Division had to cope with a flat market in Europe and severe deterioration in the commercial vehicles market in the United States," it said.

"The efforts made by the company in the area of cost reduction were not sufficient to offset the negative effects of a difficult price environment in Europe and the interruptions relating to the introduction of replacements in the company's product line," it said.

Renault's 1996 consolidated revenues were 184.08 billion francs, almost unchanged from the previous year's sales of 184.07 billion. On a like-for-like basis they slipped 0.11 percent, including a 2.3 percent gain in the car division and a 9.5 percent drop in the commercial vehicles division. ($ = 5.699 French Francs)
